column3: The Hebrew describes a staggering and a stumbling of the heart; BSB renders these images as “remorse or guilt of conscience.” It describes self-vindication with the verb for saving oneself, where BSB uses “revenge.”
The Hebrew again describes David’s own hand saving for him; BSB renders this as “avenging myself by my own hand.”
The Hebrew repeats the description “one urinating against a wall”; BSB renders it as “no male belonging to Nabal.”
The Hebrew commands going “up” to her house and uses the image “I have lifted your face.” BSB leaves the upward direction implicit and renders the face image as “granted your request.”
The Hebrew says Nabal’s heart was good within him and that she told him no small or great matter. BSB uses “in high spirits” and compresses the small-and-great pair into “nothing.”
The Hebrew describes sobriety as the wine going out of Nabal and says his heart died within him. BSB has “Nabal was sober” and “his heart failed.” It says he became a stone; BSB has “like a stone”.
The Hebrew separately says the LORD struck Nabal and that he died; BSB combines these as “struck Nabal dead.”
The Hebrew explicitly describes the reproach as coming “from Nabal’s hand”; BSB leaves the hand image implicit.
The Hebrew explicitly names “David’s servants”; BSB uses “his servants.”
The Hebrew describes the five attendants as going “at her foot”; BSB renders this as being “attended by five of her maidens.”
The Hebrew refers to both women without repeating their names; BSB supplies Abigail.
